 In the present case, Detailed Accident Report (DAR) was filed on 12.09.2022 regarding a Road Traffic Accident, which took place on 22.05.2022 at 06:00 PM at Outer Ring Road, Wazirabad Flyover, 'Y'
Point, Timar Pur, Delhi. It emerged from the DAR that on 22.05.2022,
Smt. Phoolwati along with her son-in-law Sh. Bhim Sain was going to her house from a family function and when they reached the Wazirabad Flyover, suddenly they ran out of petrol. Sh. Bhim Sain parked their vehicle on a side safely when suddenly a vehicle i.e. chhota haathi bearing registration no. DL-1L-AF-2991 driven by respondent no. 1 in a very rash and negligent manner hit the vehicle of the petitioner from the back. 
2. The vehicle bearing registration No. DL-1L-AF-2991 was being driven by respondent no.1 Mr. Aslam, owned by respondent no.2,
Mr. Alauddin and insured with respondent no.3, TATA AIG Insurance Co.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that she was taken to Lok Nayak Hospital where her MLC bearing no. 1149/2022 was prepared. 
She has deposed to have been treated by Employees State Insurance Corporation as well as Usha Dental Clinic for dental treatment as also at Metro Hospital. 
MACT No. 745/2022 Phoolwati Vs. Aslam & ors. Page 2 of 29  4. During investigation, the IO arrested the driver of the said vehicle who is the respondent no. 1, Mr. Aslam. Later, he was released on bail. Case property was seized and mechanical inspection was got conducted. The driving license of the respondent no. 1 was also got verified which was found to be a learner's license. The IO recorded the statements of all the injured persons including the petitioner. 
Chargesheet was filed under section 279/337 IPC and section 3/181 and 5/180 MV Act for driving the vehicle without a valid license. Charge- sheet/challan was filed before the concerned court of Ld. MM and DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 
5. Respondent no.1 (driver) as well as respondent no. 2 (owner) filed a common written statement on 27.02.2023 and respondent no. 3/insurance company filed its reply on 27.02.2023. 
Respondent nos.1 & 2 have stated in their written statement that they have been falsely implicated in the alleged accident and the petitioner has not come to the court with clean hands and suppressed material facts. Respondent no. 1 further stated that he has a valid driving license valid from 08.12.2021 to 07.06.2022 and he has always driven the vehicle with due care and diligence. 
6. Respondent no. 3 has stated that respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle on the basis of a learner's license but he was not accompanied by any person holding a valid driving license and thus, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify respondent nos. 1 and 2.

2 MACT No. 745/2022 Phoolwati Vs. Aslam & ors. Page 3 of 29  ISSUES FRAMED 7. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, vide order dated 27.02.2023, this Tribunal had framed the following issues:
i. Whether the petitioner Smt. Phoolwati suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 22/05/2022 at about 06:00 PM involving vehicle bearing registration No. DL-1LAF- 2991 driven by the respondent rashly and negligently, owner by the Respondent no. 2 and insured with the Respondent no. 3? OPP ii. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom? OPP iii. Relief. 
Evidence:
8. Local Commissioner was appointed for recording of evidence of the parties who filed the report on 16.01.2024. The petitioner Smt. Phoolwati was examined as PW-1 and Sh. Bhim Sain was examined as PW-2. The respondents examined Mr. Aslam as R1W2; Mr. Allauddin as R1W2 and Mr. Gulfam as R1W3. Respondent no. 3 did not lead any evidence. 
9. The petitioner filed the Form XIV. Financial statement of the petitioner was recorded. Final arguments were heard on behalf of all the parties. 
MACT No. 745/2022 Phoolwati Vs. Aslam & ors. Page 4 of 29  Findings & Observations: 
10. I have heard Ld. Counsel for the petitioner and Ld. Counsel for the respondents and perused the record. My findings on the various issues are as under:-
Issue no. 1:
Whether the petitioner Smt. Phoolwati suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 22/05/2022 at about 06:00 PM involving vehicle bearing registration No. DL-1LAF- 2991 driven by the respondent rashly and negligently, owner by the Respondent no. 2 and insured with the Respondent no. 3? OPP Phoolwati(I)(Fir 202/2022/Timar Pur) vs Aslam S/O. Aluddin on 5 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59284985/
3 11. Before delving into the facts of the current case to decide the aforementioned issues, it is pertinent to highlight that it is firmly established in legal precedents that the proceedings conducted before the Claims Tribunal are in the nature of an inquiry. Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors.
2009 ACJ 287). In civil proceedings, the establishment of facts hinges on a preponderance of probabilities, rather than being bound by the strict rules of evidence or the higher standard of beyond reasonable doubt, as required in criminal cases. The burden of proof in civil cases is lighter than in criminal cases, and the burden to decide claim petition under The Motor Vehicles Act is even lesser as compared to a civil litigation. In MACT No. 745/2022 Phoolwati Vs. Aslam & ors. Page 5 of 29  Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion. 
12. Keeping in mind the aforementioned legal principle for adjudicating the present issue, this Tribunal has thoroughly gone through the testimony of the witnesses and all the material available on record. 
Also, careful consideration has been given to the arguments addressed by the Learned Counsels for all the parties. 
The factum of accident:
13. In this matter to prove the occurrence of the accident as well as the rashness and negligence on the part of the driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1, the petitioner (PW-1) in her evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW-1/A, had deposed as under:-
 "6. That the deponent stated that on the date of  22/05/22 at around 6:00 PM. Deponent along with  her son-in-law Sh. Bheem Sain was coming to  deponent's home after attending a family function  when the deponent reached to Wazirabad Flyover,
 Delhi and suddenly the petrol of the deponent's  vehicle was consummate and son-in-law of deponent  parked their vehicle in road side safety area  suddenly the chota haathi bearing registration no.
 DL-1L-AF-2991 hit the deponent from behind in  very rash and negligent manner and hit deponent  vehicle from back side. 
 ...
8. That the deponent stated that due to rash and negligence driving of the driver this accident happened and deponent and his family suffered the loss." 
Phoolwati(I)(Fir 202/2022/Timar Pur) vs Aslam S/O. Aluddin on 5 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59284985/
4 14. The Petitioner also examined Sh. Bhim Sain as PW-2 who deposed as under:
"I am the eye witness of the accident case. On 22.05.2022 at about 6pm I along with my mother-in-law Smt. Phoolwati was coming to Phoolwati's home after attending a family function. When we reached at Wazirabad Flyover Delhi, suddenly the petrol of my vehicle was consumed and I had parked my vehicle on the side of the road after taking all the reasonable precautions. I was trying to find out the assistance of someone and my mother in law was sitting on the stationary motor cycle. Suddenly a vehicle chota hathi bearing Registration no. DL-1L-AF-2991 hit the motor cycle &
Smt. Phoolwati from behind in very rash and negligent manner. After that I immediately caught the driver of the offending vehicle and took the keys of the offending vehicle. After that I hired an auto and went to Lok Nayak hospital along with injured Smt. Phoolwati. After reaching the hospital I called 100 no. and then IO Lalit Chauhan told me to come on the accident spot and I gave my statement to the IO. Due to this accident my mother in law sustained grievous injuries on her left arm,
upper & lower lip cut, left side forehead, broken four upper teeth and multiple body injuries. This accident happened due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and my mother-in-law sustained grievous injuries." 
15. PW-1 and PW-2 have proved the factum of the accident and the identity of respondent no. 1. 
They have unequivocally testified that the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-1LAF-2991 was being driven very rashly and negligently leading to the accident in question. On the other hand,
the respondents have disputed the factum of the accident. It is the case of the respondents that respondent no. 1 along with one Gulfam was passing by the spot of accident when one person shouted, came and snatched the keys of his vehicle. It is their case that the vehicle of the respondents was not involved in any accident and thus, they are not liable. It is also their case that the petitioner was wrongly parked in the middle of the highway and thus, the respondents are not liable. To prove their version, respondents examined Mohd. Aslam as R1W1 who deposed that:
"1....on 22.05.2022, deponent alongwith Sh. Gulfam was going to Deponent's home after purchasing of some material from Mundka, Delhi. When I had reached at the flyover of Wazirabad crossing one man shouted on the road then deponent stopped his vehicle bearing no. DL-1L1F-2991.
2. That one person came to deponent and snatched deponent's vehicle key and run away from the spot in an auto-rickshaw. The deponent as well as Sh. Gulfam both was completely shocked with this incident. What happen with them? Then immediately deponent called his father and told everything about the incident and requests him to come on the spot with a spare key of the vehicle." 
16. Clearly, the depositions of PW-1 and PW-2 as to the manner of the accident and the driving of the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner by the respondent no. 1 are categorical and remained unshaken during cross-examination of the said witness and in fact was strengthened during the same. The injured/ petitioner emphatically testified that the accident occurred due to the Phoolwati(I)(Fir 202/2022/Timar Pur) vs Aslam S/O. Aluddin on 5 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59284985/
5 fault of the driver of the offending vehicle who was driving at a very high speed and hit the stationary vehicle of PW-2 upon which PW-1 was sitting. PW-2 has also clarified that he had parked the vehicle on the side of the road and thus, he was not liable in any manner. 
17. Even otherwise, the petitioner was unknown to respondent no. 1 prior to the accident and admittedly, there was no prior enmity with respondent no. 1 and hence, it is beyond comprehension as to why the petitioner will implicate the respondent no. 1 falsely, had he not been driving the offending vehicle. 
18. Even the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle shows that the front of the offending vehicle is damaged. Also, with respect to the defence raised by the respondents, it seems unbelievable that a strange person unconnected with the petitioners or the respondents will come and take the key of the respondents' vehicle. It also seems improbable that the petitioner would lie about the accident having taken place by the respondents. On the other hand, it cannot be ignored that the respondents could make a story in order to avoid liability. 
19. Furthermore, in view of filing of DAR containing the chargesheet for the offences u/s 279/337 IPC and section 5/180 and 3/181 MV Act and other relevant documents against respondent no.1 and in terms of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, respondent no.1 Mohd. Aslam (driver of the offending vehicle) is held to be negligent on the basis of preponderance of probabilities. From the DAR, it also stands established that the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-1L- AF-2991 was owned by respondent no. 2, Mohd.
Allauddin and insured with respondent no. 3, TATA AIG Insurance Co. Ltd. vide Policy No.
1622325880000 valid from 30.07.2021 to 29.07.2022. The factum of said insurance is also admitted by the respondent no.3 insurance company in its reply. 
The injury:
20. The petitioner (PW-1) testified that due to the accident, she sustained injuries on left side forehead and upper and lower lip. She is also stated to have broken four teeth and sustained multiple injuries on her body. She asserted that due to the accident, she was not in a position to do her work for 6 months. Her MLC no. 1149/22 shows that the alleged history was "RTA near Signature Bridge around 6:00 PM." and suffered injury on lower left side forehead, loss of upper incisor and lower lip. Her discharge summary and subsequent medical documents show that she has undergone treatment for dental issues also. 
21. From the above deposition and in totality of the circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner has been able to bring on record sufficient facts so as to prove at the scales of preponderance of probabilities that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration number DL-1L-AF-2991 driven by its driver/respondent no. 1 on the date and time of the accident and that due to the said accident, the petitioner had suffered injury on her forehead as well as lower and upper lips and suffered loss of teeth. Accordingly, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents. 
Phoolwati(I)(Fir 202/2022/Timar Pur) vs Aslam S/O. Aluddin on 5 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59284985/ 
6 Issue no. 2:
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom? (OPP) 
22. The onus of proving the above issue was upon the petitioner/injured. It has already been concluded in the preceding paragraphs while deciding the issue no. 1,
that the petitioner had suffered injury on her forehead and lower and upper lip. It is also proved that she suffered loss of teeth. 
23. The petitioner is certainly entitled for compensation in view of decision of the discussion on the above issues. Before proceeding further to decide the present issue,
it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases. In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under:
"General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. 
The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.
Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467). 
5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following :
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
Phoolwati(I)(Fir 202/2022/Timar Pur) vs Aslam S/O. Aluddin on 5 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59284985/
7 (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. 
(iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) 
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. 
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). 
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i),
(ii)(a) and (iv)."
24. In view of the above law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in injury cases, award needs to be passed only under heads of medical expenses, loss of earning during treatment period and damages for pain, suffering and trauma. Hence, this Tribunal now proceeds further step by step to decide the compensation/award under different heads applicable to the present matter in light of above preposition. 
Determination of Injuries and Duration of the Treatment:
25. It would be appropriate to first ascertain the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner/ injured and duration of treatment as they need to be kept in mind while ascertaining the compensation under different applicable heads. The petitioner has filed her medical record to prove her nature of injuries as per which, injured has suffered injuries on her upper lip and lower lip and has also lost some teeth. From the record, it is clear that the petitioner was admitted in the hospital on 22.05.2022 and was discharged on the intervening night of the same day. She was again admitted in Employee State Insurance Corporation Hospital on 23.05.2022 and discharged on the same day. 
She also underwent further dental treatment in Usha Dental Clinic on 02.12.2022. Now, her compensation is computed as follows:
Medical expenses:

however, in his From XIV, she has claimed medical expenses to the tune of Rs. 19,828/-. In this regard, the petitioner has placed reliance on original medical bills Ex. PW-1/6 (colly). 27. The respondents have not disputed the above medical bills. Also, the MLC mentions that the petitioner/ injured had suffered injury on her upper lip and lower lip and also lost few teeth thus,
this Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner/ injured must have incurred the above expense on her medical treatment. Therefore, an amount of Rs. 9,963/- is awarded to the petitioner/ injured Phoolwati towards medical expenses. 
Loss of income:
28. Coming to the aspect of loss of income, the petitioner Phoolwati claimed that she was working in a private job in an iron factory and was earning Rs. 20,000/- per month, but due to the accident in question she could not work for 6 months and suffered complete loss of earnings during that period. 
However, the petitioner has not filed any document to show that she was working in an iron factory or that she was earning Rs.20,000/- per month. Moreover, considering the injury of the Petitioner,
it does not seem that the petitioner would have suffered any loss of income. Thus, she is not held entitled to any amount under this head. 
Mental shock:
29. The petitioner/ injured has claimed Rs. 50,000/- under this head, however, there is no cogent evidence on record regarding the same. However, taking into account the injuries suffered by her,
Rs.5,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head of mental shock. 
Pain and Suffering:
30. The petitioner/ injured has claim Rs. 1,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering, however, no justification has been given for claiming such a huge amount. It is true that a particular amount cannot be fixed under the head pain and suffering which could be applicable to all cases as it varies Phoolwati(I)(Fir 202/2022/Timar Pur) vs Aslam S/O. Aluddin on 5 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59284985/
10 from case to case. Judicial notice can be taken of the fact that since the petitioner has received certain injuries, therefore, petitioner must have suffered pain and sufferings owing to the said injuries. Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner as mentioned in the MLC, this Tribunal hereby grants compensation of Rs. 5,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner. 
Special Diet:
31. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 50,000/- under the head special diet but there is no cogent evidence on record regarding money spent by the petitioner upon special diet. However, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner must have spent some money under this head. Hence, this Tribunal hereby grant compensation of Rs. 5,000/- towards expenses incurred on special diet. 
Conveyance charges:
32. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 50,000/- under the head conveyance charges but there is no cogent evidence for the same. However, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner must have incurred some expense on conveyance. Hence, this Tribunal hereby grant compensation of Rs. 5,000/- towards conveyance charges. 
Attendant charges:
33. The petitioner/ injured has claimed Rs. 50,000/- under this head, however, there is no cogent evidence on record for the money spent by the petitioner upon an attendant. However, taking into account the injuries suffered by him, Rs. 5,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head of attendant charges. 
Future treatment:
34. The petitioner has claimed expense towards future treatment, however, she has not filed any document to show that she could incur further expense on her treatment. Thus, she is held not entitled to any amount under this head.

annotations.text: The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

(See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.

summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors.
2009 ACJ 287).
In civil proceedings, the establishment of facts hinges on a preponderance of probabilities, rather than being bound by the strict rules of evidence or the higher standard of beyond reasonable doubt, as required in criminal cases.
The burden of proof in civil cases is lighter than in criminal cases, and the burden to decide claim petition under The Motor Vehicles Act is even lesser as compared to a civil litigation.
In MACT No. 745/2022 Phoolwati Vs. Aslam & ors. Page 5 of 29  Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion.

15. PW-1 and PW-2 have proved the factum of the accident and the identity of respondent no. 1.

They have unequivocally testified that the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-1LAF-2991 was being driven very rashly and negligently leading to the accident in question.
On the other hand,
the respondents have disputed the factum of the accident.
It is the case of the respondents that respondent no. 1 along with one Gulfam was passing by the spot of accident when one person shouted, came and snatched the keys of his vehicle.
It is their case that the vehicle of the respondents was not involved in any accident and thus, they are not liable.
It is also their case that the petitioner was wrongly parked in the middle of the highway and thus, the respondents are not liable.
16. Clearly, the depositions of PW-1 and PW-2 as to the manner of the accident and the driving of the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner by the respondent no. 1 are categorical and remained unshaken during cross-examination of the said witness and in fact was strengthened during the same.
The injured/ petitioner emphatically testified that the accident occurred due to the Phoolwati(I)(Fir 202/2022/Timar Pur) vs Aslam S/O. Aluddin on 5 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59284985/
5 fault of the driver of the offending vehicle who was driving at a very high speed and hit the stationary vehicle of PW-2 upon which PW-1 was sitting.
17. Even otherwise, the petitioner was unknown to respondent no. 1 prior to the accident and admittedly, there was no prior enmity with respondent no. 1 and hence, it is beyond comprehension as to why the petitioner will implicate the respondent no. 1 falsely, had he not been driving the offending vehicle.
18. Even the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle shows that the front of the offending vehicle is damaged.
Also, with respect to the defence raised by the respondents, it seems unbelievable that a strange person unconnected with the petitioners or the respondents will come and take the key of the respondents' vehicle.
It also seems improbable that the petitioner would lie about the accident having taken place by the respondents.
On the other hand, it cannot be ignored that the respondents could make a story in order to avoid liability.
19. Furthermore, in view of filing of DAR containing the chargesheet for the offences u/s 279/337 IPC and section 5/180 and 3/181 MV Act and other relevant documents against respondent no.1 and in terms of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, respondent no.1 Mohd. Aslam (driver of the offending vehicle) is held to be negligent on the basis of preponderance of probabilities.
21. From the above deposition and in totality of the circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner has been able to bring on record sufficient facts so as to prove at the scales of preponderance of probabilities that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration number DL-1L-AF-2991 driven by its driver/respondent no. 1 on the date and time of the accident and that due to the said accident, the petitioner had suffered injury on her forehead as well as lower and upper lips and suffered loss of teeth.
While the respondent no. 1 has examined himself as well as Mr. Gulfam to prove that Mr.
Gulfam was accompanying him in the offending vehicle at the time of the accident, the insurance company has not brought forward any concrete evidence to prove otherwise.
It is settled law that the present proceedings are in the nature of an inquiry and a fact is not required to be proved to the hilt.

Also, the nature of the present proceedings is beneficial in nature and thus, the facts as well as the depositions should be read in a positive light only to advance the cause of justice.
Further, the duty of the insurance company is to indemnify the insured unless there is a gross violation of one of its terms.
In the present case, the respondent no. 1 has been able to prove on the balance of probabilities that Mr. Gulfam, holder of a valid driving license, was accompanying him at the time of the accident.
Thus, considering the depositions of the witnesses as well as the underlying object of the Act, this Tribunal is of the view that respondent no.3/insurance company is liable to indemnify respondent nos.1 and 2 for the award amount.
